verdict: Arm B argues better on evidence and verification: it tests the proposed remedy against the code (LB13, LB14, LA8, LB21, LA20, LA4), cites the shipped master version as independent confirmation, corrects its own findings' weaker sub-claims (LB11, LB12, LB18, LA19), and writes 20-word sentences with one idea each, though it pays in length (median 335 vs 290 words) and twice rejects on a premise the same run refutes (LA10 against LA11/LA13, LB10 against LB8). Arm A cites densely and finds good in-repo precedents (NA6, NA15, NA21, NB16) and test fixtures (NA2, NA14), but its 33-word sentences chain several ideas each, it contradicts itself inside one run more often (NA1 against NA8/NA13, NA5 and NA22 against NA7/NA10/NA11, NB12 against NB17), reads master's later fixes as the pre-PR base in NA1 and NA14, points readers at unresolvable sibling ids, and many blocks close by restating the reviewer's severity instead of testing it; pair tally: B wins 20 (7 marginal), A wins 2, 7 ties.
